origins: This belief often follows a long run of hardship: repeated losses, chronic illness, financial struggles, or a childhood where good things rarely lasted. When disappointment comes again and again, the mind learns to expect it, partly to avoid being caught off guard. Over time hopelessness can feel like realism, and good things get dismissed as flukes.
teaches: Scripture does not deny that life brings trouble, but it insists that trouble is not the final word. God told His people in exile that He had plans to give them a future and a hope. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning. God promises to do new things, even making a way in the wilderness. Paul wrote that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him. Bad seasons are real, but they are seasons, and God is at work in them.
self_statements: Nothing ever works out for me.
As soon as things get better, something will ruin it.
Why hope? It never turns out.
My life is just one bad thing after another.
It will always be like this.
errors: Predicting that the future will be as bad as the past.
Seeing only what goes wrong and overlooking what goes right.
Calling good things luck or temporary.
questions: Is it true that things always go badly, or only often?
What has gone well, even in small ways, this past year?
What season of my life was better than I expected?
What does God say about my future?
Am I protecting myself from disappointment by expecting the worst?
What would hope look like today?
truth: I have been through many hard things, and more may come. But “always” is not true. Good things have happened, and God has promised a future and a hope. Hard seasons do not last forever, and God is at work even now.
hw_truths: God has plans to give me a future and a hope.
His mercies are new every morning.
Good things are real, not just luck.
log: Each evening, write three things that went right today, even small ones.
actions: Each night for two weeks, write three good things that happened. Read the whole list at the end.
Write about a time something you dreaded turned out better than expected.
Schedule one small thing you can look forward to this week.
If hopelessness is heavy or constant, talk with a doctor, pastor, or counselor.
prayer: Lord, I have come to expect the worst. Thank You that You have plans to give me a future and a hope. Open my eyes to the good You are doing, and give me hope for tomorrow. Amen.
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Things will always go badly.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
